solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Luxurious hotel's abandoned asset

indicators.note: something abandoned has been left behind, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: plush means richly comfortable
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grand hotel has let one of its valuable properties go to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUSH loses its H to leave PLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or good point, so an asset in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Side that's after Arsenal's wingers

parts.note: later means afterwards

indicators.note: wingers play on the edges of the pitch, so the outer letters of the word are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of the club's name; Arsenal is a London football club

explanation.surface: A football team is pursuing an opponent's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Lateral is also a noun, a sideways pass or branch, so it can stand for side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral relates to the sides of something, and as a noun names a side part, branch or sideways pass.

clue.text: Burst lotion almost beginning to ooze

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: salve, a healing ointment, without its last letter

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tube of cream nearly splits open and starts seeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a burst of fire, or figuratively a sudden burst of applause.

clue.text: Upset all odds and catch one?

definitions.text: Upset all odds and catch one?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
odds asks for the letters in the odd positions of the preceding word

parts.note: first and third letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Landing a certain fish would be a tremendous stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the coelacanth was thought extinct for millions of years until one was caught in 1938, against all odds.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient lobe-finned fish was believed long extinct, so catching a living specimen defied every expectation.

clue.text: Fish basket that's gone rotten inside

indicators.note: rotten means decayed and broken down, so these letters fall into a new order
inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket
the word gone with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler's catch has gone off in the basket.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten looks like it describes the fish, but it signals rearranging the word before it, which then sits inside the basket.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger eel is a large marine eel, and eels are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Bird unable to fly behind mirror

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: A flightless bird stands behind a looking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mirror looks like a noun here, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror someone is to copy or imitate them closely, which is what emulating means.

clue.text: A college not displaying its old spirit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not displaying means keeping hidden, so that letter is left out

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An Oxford college has stopped showing its traditional ethos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' ties the missing letter to the college's own name, so the old abbreviation is removed from that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest, a famous spirit of literature.

clue.text: It's unwise to force a climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: silly means foolish
to ram is to force or push hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pushing a creeper to grow is foolish gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' reads as one phrase, a creeper, but climbing is the instruction and plant alone is the definition. SILLY RAM A read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a bulb with large trumpet-shaped flowers, so a flowering plant.

clue.text: Tropical tree deserted by its last monkey

indicators.note: abandoned by its final letter, so the end of the word is removed

parts.note: the tamarind is a tropical tree bearing sour pods

explanation.surface: A monkey has abandoned its last refuge, a jungle tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American primate related to marmosets, a kind of monkey.

clue.text: Hot bread one left out

indicators.note: left out means omitted, so one of these letters is not used

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit bread eaten at Christmas
L is the abbreviation for left; only one of the two is removed

explanation.surface: Someone has left out a warm loaf, and with it one of its ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: STOLLEN has two Ls, and dropping one gives STOLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen goods, as in a hot car that a thief has taken.

clue.text: Indignant child may be raised here?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a child is lifted and held in a parent's embrace

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of an idiom; the phrase is usually figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people who are furiously protesting, as if they had taken up weapons against something.

clue.text: Special gardens suffered in a motoring accident

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: RTA is the British abbreviation for a road traffic accident
bore is the past tense of bear, to suffer or endure

explanation.surface: Some fine gardens were damaged when a car crashed into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motoring accident' looks like scene-setting, but it is the standard British abbreviation for a road traffic accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreta, plural of arboretum, are botanical gardens devoted to growing trees, so a specialised kind of garden.

clue.text: Actors wanting the lead in films

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and the lead is the first letter, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: players are performers on stage

explanation.surface: A cast of performers is waiting to be given the starring role in some movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lead in films' reads as a starring role, but films is the definition and in only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Films in the sense of thin coatings or sheets laid over something are layers, such as a film of oil.

clue.text: Avoid spring visiting desert unescorted

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to desert is to leave
without company
a spring is a natural source of water, as is a well

explanation.surface: Steer clear of an oasis when crossing the desert on your own.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert looks like a noun, sandy wasteland, but it is the verb meaning to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something well alone is to refrain from interfering with it, keeping away or steering clear.

clue.text: Hero soon has bold maiden imprisoned

indicators.note: has, together with imprisoned, means holds captive inside, so the pieces go within
something imprisoned is shut inside, completing the split instruction to enclose

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
game means plucky or willing
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A legendary hero will shortly have a brave young woman locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The containment instruction is split around the pieces: has at the start and imprisoned at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king who led the Greeks at Troy, a central hero of Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: They're steamy in Paris, the king wears lingerie

parts.note: la is French for the

indicators.note: something worn is put on around the wearer, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: undies is informal for underwear
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A racy Parisian scene where the monarch dons ladies' underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Steamy suggests something racy, but it is literal: these places are full of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundries are full of hot water and steam from washing and pressing clothes, so they are literally steamy.

clue.text: A sailor they say runs tests for soldiers

indicators.note: they say points to how words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
a river runs or courses along

explanation.surface: A seaman reportedly organises exams for army recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault course is an obstacle circuit on which military trainees are tested for fitness and agility.

clue.text: Expect to be affected by drink

parts.note: to sup is to sip or drink
to pose is to behave affectedly, putting on airs

explanation.surface: You would expect drinking to have an effect on you.
explanation.walkthrough: By marks POSE as placed beside SUP, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or think likely, which is what expecting something means.

clue.text: Where bats display evidence of iron deficiency?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, the marked lines at which batsmen stand and show their skill
second meaning: wrinkles in clothes that have not been pressed

explanation.surface: Something about flying mammals and the signs of anaemia.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats are batsmen and iron is the household appliance, not the mineral; the medical reading is a false scent.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the batting and popping lines are called creases, and fabric wrinkles show clothes went unpressed.

clue.text: Tax period

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to strain or push to the limit
second meaning: a continuous span of time

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a tax year, but tax here means to strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch resources is to tax them hard, and a stretch is an unbroken spell of time, including a prison term.

clue.text: Draw a ring round the capital of Peru

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one part goes around the other

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the country

explanation.surface: Sketch a circle around Lima on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Peru' tempts with Lima, but here capital means the first letter. P goes inside A PEAL: A(P)PEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw people is to attract them, and to appeal is to be attractive or interesting to them.

clue.text: Room register

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to submit formally, as with a complaint

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns, a room and a register at a hotel desk, but both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To room somewhere is to stay as a paying guest, and one may formally submit or file a complaint.

clue.text: Finish fish, squeezing over piece of fruit

indicators.note: squeezing means holding tightly between, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the end is the finish
a freshwater fish
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Clear your plate of the fish course, then press it before dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of fruit' suggests a whole apple or pear, but here it means one botanical part of a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocarp is the innermost layer of a fruit's wall, such as the stone of a cherry, so one part of it.

clue.text: Sort of ocean craft

indicators.note: sort can mean arrange, so these letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A type of seagoing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of ocean craft' reads as a kind of boat, but sort of is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand, and craft is a general word for boats.

clue.text: They blow rent knocking back drink

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn

indicators.note: knocking back means turning backwards here, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: Tenants blow their rent money downing drinks at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like a payment to a landlord, but it is the past of rend. Knocking back looks like drinking, but it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tornadoes are violent whirling windstorms, so they blow; this plural spelling without the E is also accepted.

clue.text: Present at birth tucked away behind tavern

indicators.note: behind says one piece follows after the other

parts.note: a pub or tavern
to tuck away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A newborn's gift is eaten in a quiet corner behind the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn rather than learned, existing in someone from the very start of life.

clue.text: Parties of runners, maybe drinking quickly to absorb energy

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: runner beans are one kind of bean, hence maybe

indicators.note: absorbing soaks something up inside, so a piece is enclosed

parts.note: fast means quickly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Athletes at their celebrations gulp drinks down for an energy boost.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners suggests athletes, but it means runner beans. E goes into FAST, and that goes into BEANS: BEAN(F(E)AST)S.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is an informal British word for a jolly celebration or party, often a works outing.

clue.text: Genuine Caravaggio's first shown in the retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word is read in the other direction
shown in means placed within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the painter's name

parts.note: first letter of the painter's name

explanation.surface: An authentic Caravaggio, his earliest work, hangs in an exhibition looking back on his career.
explanation.walkthrough: Retrospective looks like an art exhibition, but it signals reading the word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German borrowing used in English for authentic or real, the true article.
